clue.text: Rough guides for those needing a lift?

definitions.text: Rough guides for those needing a lift?

parts.words: Rough guides for those needing a lift?
parts.note: practical rough guides, read as rules for hitchhikers, who stick out a digit to beg a ride

explanation.surface: Seems to describe travel guidebooks written for people hoping to hitch a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough guides' are approximate rules; the second half playfully suggests a hitchhiker's raised thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximate practical principles are commonly called by this idiom, here also hinted at hitchhikers.

clue.text: Resort merges restricting island systems

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the rearranged letters surround the island letter
resort read as re-sort, so the letters of merges are sorted again

explanation.surface: A holiday resort merges, limiting the island's arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot but is the anagram signal, read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling arrangements or systems of government; plural nouns both.

clue.text: Curtains may be so connected with no end of work

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the picked letter is taken out

parts.note: linked means connected

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Curtains attached to each other with the job left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains are often backed with an extra layer of fabric, described by this word.

clue.text: Second offence will include periodical brawl

indicators.note: will include means will contain, so the periodical goes inside the offence

parts.note: a crime is an offence
mag, short for magazine, is a periodical

explanation.surface: A repeat offence involving a magazine ends in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused tussle or scuffle; noun synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow left work a failure

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A man walked out of his job, a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a dud or fiasco, especially a show that bombs.

clue.text: The man's Italian and worker's uncertain

parts.note: he's is a short form of 'the man is'
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A man of Italy and a labourer are both unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsure or wavering; adjectives with the same meaning.

clue.text: Time in simple measure

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the word for simple

parts.note: mere means simple, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Time kept in a plain rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length, or a poetic rhythm; either way a measure.

clue.text: Chance of Ant and Dec being relocated around the Channel Islands?

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the islands' abbreviation
relocated means moved to new places, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
CI abbreviates Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Wonders whether the TV double act might move to the Channel Islands by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting duo; the Channel Islands lie off the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chance in the sense of luck or something unplanned; noun synonyms.

clue.text: Street's houses get old steps

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the street pieces surround the verb

parts.note: ST abbreviates street, and the 's adds S
to age is to get old

explanation.surface: The houses on a road grow worn, as do its steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Phases or periods in a process; plural noun synonyms.

clue.text: Giant injured groin with sumo wrestling

indicators.note: an injured body part is knocked out of shape, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wrestling twists and grapples, a second hint that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge wrestler has hurt his groin during a sumo bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means enormous, and this is a slangy word for very big.

clue.text: Understood source of interest in diplomacy

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: diplomacy is tact, skill in handling people

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Reads as a comment on what drives interest in diplomatic affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood without being stated outright is implied, or unspoken.

clue.text: A mistake, vacuously chasing crazy Frenchwoman

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so these pieces follow the word for crazy

parts.note: crazy means mad

indicators.note: vacuously means emptily, so the word mistake loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A blunder made while pursuing a deranged Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French title for a married lady, so it can stand for a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Saying that's popular within total golf

parts.note: total, as in a total disaster, means utter
in means popular, fashionable
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Seems to praise a popular saying about the game of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something aloud is voicing or speaking it; both are present participles.

clue.text: Greeting mother, regrettably coming back

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the two words are read from right to left

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
alas is an exclamation meaning regrettably

explanation.surface: A sad greeting given to a mother who is returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a low bow of respectful salutation in Arabic and Muslim custom.

clue.text: This may be canned and used as medicine, proverbially

definitions.text: This may be canned and used as medicine, proverbially

parts.words: This may be canned and used as medicine, proverbially
parts.note: sitcoms add a recorded audience reaction, and a well-known proverb calls this the best medicine

explanation.surface: Sounds like a preserved remedy, recommended by an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded audience chuckles are canned, and the saying calls merriment the best medicine.

clue.text: Critics of these often found on the door

definitions.meaning: people who constantly find fault and run things down

definitions.text: these often found on the door
definitions.meaning: hinged metal rappers fixed to front doors for visitors to bang

explanation.surface: Suggests critics hammering at someone's front door.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for detractors, and also the hinged metal devices visitors rap on a front door.

clue.text: Happy to cross one new area of our planet

indicators.note: to cross means to straddle, so the happy word stretches around the others

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Content to traverse a fresh region of the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is one of the great land masses of Earth.

clue.text: A container like this is needed for prickly plant

parts.note: a can is a container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: Advice that a pot of this sort suits a thorny plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny-leaved Mediterranean plant, also the model for Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Wealth of guild regularly viewed in old money

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the old money

parts.note: pence is British small money

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of guild is taken

explanation.surface: A guild's wealth reckoned in pre-decimal coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Great wealth and luxurious abundance; a noun synonym for riches.

clue.text: Fruit and duck on kitchen stove

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the duck above the stove

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O
a range is a large kitchen cooker

explanation.surface: Evokes duck à l'orange cooking on the hob.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus fruit; the answer is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Poles must anticipate urge to grass

indicators.note: anticipate means come before, so the poles are placed in front of the urge

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles
an itch is an urge or craving

explanation.surface: Polish people feel compelled to inform on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'grass' is British slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang verbs for informing on someone to the authorities.

clue.text: Unfortunate student in poor shape finishes at last

indicators.note: in puts the student letter inside the others
poor means in bad condition, so these letters are rearranged
at last points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: L, a learner driver's plate, is a student

explanation.surface: A learner out of condition finally comes off badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes HAPES from SHAPE; the S from 'finishes' follows, and L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlucky or ill-starred; adjective synonyms.

clue.text: The girl's in a depression, being a follower

indicators.note: in places the word for the girl inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface
her refers to the girl; the 's reads as 'is' and joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A young woman, feeling low, becomes someone's disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or devotee of a cause or person; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Horseman's answer ignored by attacker

indicators.note: ignored by means left out of, so the letter is dropped from the attacker

parts.note: a raider is an attacker

explanation.surface: A cavalryman's reply goes unheeded by an assailant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Horseman' reads as 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sits on and rides a horse, a mounted traveller.

clue.text: Enough to satisfy head of Interpol before power boost

indicators.note: before puts these pieces ahead of the letter for power

parts.note: one's fill is as much as satisfies

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A police agency chief is given enough to satisfy him before a boost in power.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus or encouragement; the two words are noun synonyms.

clue.text: Partly fill an order that's plain

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fulfilling a purchase only in part, which is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy treeless plain of South America, especially Venezuela.

clue.text: Stick around a Pacific island

indicators.note: around puts the stick word on both sides of the single letter

parts.note: gum is a sticky substance, and to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Stay near an island in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: A US territory in the western Pacific, the largest island of the Marianas.

clue.text: Good communist limits Eastern hunger

indicators.note: limits means bounds on both sides, so the communist word surrounds the letter for Eastern

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist

explanation.surface: A decent communist puts a check on Eastern hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid craving for more, as in a hunger for power; noun synonyms.

clue.text: Person who shares Spooner's dislike of rodents?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals the opening sounds of two words swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent
to hate is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: Asks for a flatmate who also can't stand mice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares a dwelling with you; the definition leaves the shared home understood.

clue.text: Pair (English) confronting extravagant forward

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so these pieces stand in front of the extravagant word

parts.note: sumptuous means lavish or extravagant

explanation.surface: Describes an English pair facing a lavish front-line player.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward meaning overconfident or presumptive in manner; adjective synonyms.
